audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer told the reader 'your ball is not a projectile, so his Wind Wall does nothing to your Q, W or R - a huge tempo win'. That is false, and it directly contradicts the full layer's own TL;DR ('Wind Wall eats the ball mid-flight').
audit.why: Orianna's Q carries the projectile flag in Riot's kit data and Wind Wall blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds. The ball's Q travel is blocked; W and R fire from wherever the ball already sits, which is why the correct advice is to place the ball around the wall or on yourself, not to ignore the wall.
audit.corrected: spikes[0].text, early and wants.you[0] rewritten to say the wall blocks the Q on the way out and that a parked ball still pulses W and R. The two layers now agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart gave Yasuo all seven rows at 7/10; the content layer and the packet levelChart both read Orianna, Skill x5, Orianna.
audit.why: Level 1 he has 475-range Steel Tempest and no wall; late, an AoE Shockwave outvalues a single-target dive. The middle of the game is genuinely even and both other sources say so.
audit.corrected: All seven full sides moved onto the content/packet verdict with whys and ratings rewritten to match. win[] already held the correct tokens.

edits.after: - Wind Wall (W): 25s at rank 1, 17s at rank 5, and 4 seconds of blocking — it eats your Q, so poke around it or wait it out. - Sweeping Blade (E): near-zero cooldown, but it cannot re-target the same unit for a few seconds. - Your R at 110s answers his engage.

edits.before: Yasuo's whole plan is stacking Steel Tempest (Q) to a tornado and E-dashing through the wave to all-in on the knockup. Crucially your ball is not a projectile, so his Wind Wall (W) does nothing to your Q, W or R - a huge tempo win. Trade with ball harass when his E is on a minion cooldown, and don't stand in a full caster wave where he can E-gapclose for free.
edits.after: Yasuo's whole plan is stacking Steel Tempest (Q) to a tornado and E-dashing through the wave to all-in on the knockup. Wind Wall (W) blocks your Q on the way out, so place the ball around the wall or leave it on yourself - once parked, W and R still fire from it. Trade when his E is on its per-target lockout, and never sit in a full caster wave.

edits.after: Level 1 is yours - your ball out-ranges his 475-range Steel Tempest and he has no Wind Wall yet, so take the free harass. Land Q-W before he stacks a tornado, and from level 2 aim the ball around the wall instead of into it.

notes: The most serious defect in this matchup was factual, not cosmetic: the content layer claimed Orianna's ball is not a projectile and that Wind Wall does nothing to it. Riot's kit data flags her Q as a projectile and Wind Wall blocks all enemy projectiles for 4 seconds, and the full layer's own TL;DR said the opposite of the content layer. Fixed on the content side so both layers agree. All seven chart rows disagreed across layers (full had Yasuo x7); the full layer was moved onto the content/packet verdict. Left alone and worth a look: diff is HARD 8/10 while the chart and a 50.36% win rate over 2659 games read even — I did not have grounds in the kit to move the rating.
